rule: GOAL: Guide the falling block into a waiting cup. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blue paddle; space releases the block. RULE: The paddle deflects the block mid-air to steer it into the cup. TRAP: Trying to push the block sideways before it falls wastes moves; release it first, then steer.

GOAL: Move the square along the dotted path to reach the circle. CONTROLS: Click ahead to slide the square a short distance along the line of dots. RULE: You can only move as far as the visible dots allow; the path is fixed. TRAP: Thinking you could click far ahead; overreaching fails and wastes time, so stick to short hops.

GOAL: Navigate a grid to reach the exit within a strict step limit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character exactly two cells in that direction. RULE: Each move jumps two spaces, requiring both the intermediate and destination cells to be clear. TRAP: Assuming standard one-cell movement or sliding until blocked wastes steps and misleads pathfinding.

GOAL: Drop the plug into the bottom socket by setting the correct travel distance. CONTROLS: Click horizontal or vertical bars to toggle them black; click the large circle to launch the plug. RULE: Each fully black T-section adds four rows of downward movement to the plug's path. TRAP: Believing partial black bars count as active; only fully black sections contribute to the distance.

GOAL: Align the yellow plug directly beneath the yellow marker in the black bar. CONTROLS: Click the top blue block to shift the gray shape left; click the bottom block to reverse the shift. RULE: The total horizontal width of the gray shape remains constant at 84 units during every move. TRAP: Assuming the shape rotates or shears in 3D; it actually translates horizontally while preserving its total width.

GOAL: Guide the glowing dot on the bar tip to land precisely on the cross's center. CONTROLS: Click the plus panel to extend the bar three cells at a time. RULE: The dot sits one cell behind the tip, so overshoot by one to hit the target. TRAP: Assuming the tip must touch the cross wastes moves; the dot must reach the center instead.

GOAL: Align the bS plug to fit the narrow channel. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the plug left or right. RULE: Movement shifts position; initial movement rotates orientation. TRAP: Believing every move rotates the plug; it only rotated once.

GOAL: Match the pink dial to the blue target in every column. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows move the cursor. Up and down arrows rotate the dial. RULE: The dial follows a specific hidden cycle order, not numerical sequence. TRAP: Assuming down decreases the number wastes time; always check the cycle position first.

GOAL: Align the green plug directly beneath the green marker in the middle bar. CONTROLS: Clicking the middle band shifts its green section right; clicking the bottom band shifts it left. RULE: The middle green width must equal the bottom green width to center the plug perfectly under the marker. TRAP: Ignoring the top band’s width, which acts as a counterweight limiting how far the middle can shift.

GOAL: Push the plug up through the shaft to the handle. CONTROLS: Click white cells to charge; use arrow keys to move the plug. RULE: The plug fits the narrow channel only after being charged. TRAP: Thinking the plug needs shrinking; it only needs correct alignment and charge to slide up.

GOAL: Align the yellow row to the target sequence by cycling each column to its correct glyph state. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selection cursor; UP cycled the glyph in the selected column through its rotation states. RULE: The yellow row sat between the two bracket markers, identifying it as the active dial row to adjust. TRAP: Assuming the pink row was the dial because it looked prominent, when the brackets strictly defined the yellow row as interactive.

GOAL: Translate the yellow glyph row into a matching blue row by applying specific grouping rules. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; other inputs adjust the blue glyph under the cursor to match the target. RULE: Yellow sequences map to blue sequences via fixed groupings, such as three yellows becoming one blue. TRAP: Assuming yellow and blue rows have equal length; they do not, as some rules change the count.

GOAL: Move two pieces to touch edges and merge into one. CONTROLS: Clicking a spot shifts the nearest piece toward that click. RULE: A piece moves if the click is within its reach; diagonal shifts are allowed. TRAP: Assuming only straight moves work; diagonals are valid and often faster.

GOAL: Shift energy to specific bands while respecting capacity limits. CONTROLS: Click a band to pull two units from an adjacent neighbor. RULE: A band cannot exceed its maximum height, blocking transfers if full. TRAP: Assuming you can push energy into a full band; it silently fails, wasting moves.

GOAL: Guide the plug into the ring's open socket to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the plug four cells per press. RULE: The plug snaps into place only when touching the gray core. TRAP: Believing the plug stops at obstacles; it halts entirely if the full step is blocked.

GOAL: The level required filling three specific frame slots using a single box. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the player and attached box; Space picked up or dropped the cargo. RULE: The box occupies the cell directly behind the player, blocking movement if it hits obstacles. TRAP: Assuming the box only blocks the player’s path, ignoring that it collides with static objects ahead during transit.

ESTABLISHED: The legend's R icon changed to a hollow ring, marking the first slot as filled. The R block remains visible at its position. The tail tip is currently threaded through the R block. FAILED: Pressing LEFT to detach the tail did not cause the R block to disappear or move, nor did it update the legend further. GOAL IS NOT: The goal is not for collected blocks to vanish immediately upon reaching the slot or upon tail detachment. CONTROLS: LEFT retracts the tail and detaches it from threaded blocks; DOWN moves the cursor to a new band; RIGHT pushes blocks into the tail.

GOAL: Match the bottom row of yellow tiles to the target sequence derived from the legend chain. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; pressing an arrow rotates the selected tile up or down the color cycle. RULE: Only tiles matching the four specific legend yellow types count; other colors are decoys. TRAP: Assuming all visible yellow tiles were targets wasted time trying to match decoy colors.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit without being caught by the red enemy. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step in that direction. RULE: The enemy charges along your row if you are close, so avoid lateral proximity. TRAP: Assuming the red block is static; it moves aggressively, making vertical escapes risky if you linger in its line of sight.

GOAL: Move pieces to merge them into a target shape. CONTROLS: Clicking sets a piece’s center to that spot. RULE: Pieces only move if the distance is within nine steps. TRAP: Clicking the destination edge causes overshoot; aim for the exact center.

GOAL: Arrange colored tokens in the box to match the specific color sequence shown in the top row. CONTROLS: Click a color in the side palette to select it, then click a slot in the box to place it. RULE: The top row acts as a fixed legend, dictating the exact left-to-right order for the empty slots below. TRAP: Assuming the gray dot is a playable color or that placed tokens can be rearranged freely within slots.

GOAL: Clear the level by destroying all three red enemies using exactly nineteen actions. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character to navigate the grid and attack enemies. RULE: Enemies only attack if you are directly in their facing line of sight. TRAP: Assuming enemies attack in all directions causes unnecessary deaths; they only strike forward.

GOAL: Align two colored crosses so their lines pass through matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active cross; Space switches between colors. RULE: Each cross must cover its own color’s dots to clear the level. TRAP: Assuming one cross could solve all dots, or that switching colors resets progress.

GOAL: Move the purple square onto the purple ring. CONTROLS: Clicking moves the white diamond to the cursor; clicking the gray diamond swaps their positions. RULE: The square always sits exactly at the midpoint between the white and gray diamonds. TRAP: Assuming you can drag the square directly; you must maneuver the diamonds to position the square.

GOAL: Position blocks on target slots and pack them tightly together on the same row. CONTROLS: Arrows move the snake's head; the tail follows and drags any block it is currently touching. RULE: You only move blocks by threading the snake's body through them and pulling. TRAP: Believing blocks stay attached after you detach them; they do not, so you must re-thread and pull in one continuous motion.

GOAL: Rotate the ring so letters align with the pipe entry point. CONTROLS: Click a letter to select it, click a slot to move or swap pieces, press space to test flow. RULE: The pipe only connects to the specific slot directly below its stem, requiring precise alignment. TRAP: Assuming any adjacent slot works for the pipe connection, wasting moves on misaligned letters.

GOAL: Carry the rotated piece to the box entrance. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; stepping on crosses flips orientation. RULE: The player’s shape must match the socket’s profile to fit. TRAP: Assuming the box was a solid wall; it is a lock waiting for the correct key.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align green slots, then shift colored blocks into the matching bottom border gaps. CONTROLS: Left-click selects a piece, left-click places it or swaps with another, and Space confirms the solution. RULE: Pieces can only move into adjacent empty slots or directly swap positions with other pieces. TRAP: Assuming pieces must slide one step at a time; direct swaps between any two visible pieces save many actions.

GOAL: Move three distinct shapes to align with their matching colored dot clusters. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active shape; Spacebar switches which shape is currently active. RULE: Only the currently selected shape responds to movement commands, requiring you to cycle through them to position each one. TRAP: Assuming the active shape remains the same after pressing Space, or trying to move all shapes simultaneously with a single direction.

GOAL: Align the yellow block with the yellow cursor marker. CONTROLS: Click left or right arrows to rotate the ring of blocks clockwise or counter-clockwise. RULE: The ring rotates as a whole; only relative position between the block and cursor matters. TRAP: Believing the top dashes limited moves or that specific slots needed matching colors.

GOAL: Move two starting balls through separate maze branches until they meet and merge into a single block at the top corridor. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move both balls simultaneously in mirrored directions; Spacebar has no effect on movement. RULE: The puzzle is solved the moment the two balls occupy the same space and combine into one larger unit. TRAP: Do not attempt to navigate the merged block to a specific slot or rotate it; merging is the only requirement for completion.

GOAL: Move pegs by jumping over neighbors to clear the board. CONTROLS: Click a peg to highlight valid moves, then click the landing spot to jump. Use UNDO to reverse the last move. RULE: A peg jumps over an adjacent peg into an empty hole, removing the jumped peg. TRAP: Believing UNDO restores the board after multiple moves; it often only reverses the immediate last action or fails if the state is softlocked.

GOAL: Arrange seven colored tokens to match a hidden sequence while navigating a nested sub-box. CONTROLS: Click tokens to select, click slots to place, and press space to confirm the layout. RULE: A ring marker inserts the sub-box at that position, shifting subsequent tokens to later sequence numbers. TRAP: Assuming the ring’s slot still holds a token; it actually consumes the position, forcing later pieces to shift.

GOAL: Turn grid D’s cells red to match the pattern shown in its center icon. CONTROLS: Click individual cells to change their color. RULE: The center icon acts as a legend; white spots indicate where red cells belong. TRAP: Thinking the icon was just decoration or a cursor, rather than the specific target pattern for the active grid.

GOAL: Move three shapes to cover all dots. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape. Space switches to the next shape. RULE: Each shape must align perfectly with its assigned dots to count as covered. TRAP: Moving a shape away from its target before covering it wastes moves; plan the path to the final position first.

GOAL: Arrange colored tiles into matching red and blue boxes using a specific sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click boxes to place, press space to confirm. RULE: Blue boxes require the exact tile pattern found in the target sequence. TRAP: Assuming rings could be placed anywhere; they only fit slots where the target sequence allows a gap.

GOAL: Match the grid to two overlapping icon patterns by setting cells to orange. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between blue and orange. RULE: White in the icons means orange, gray means blue; the icons overlap on the middle row. TRAP: Assuming the target color is red like the previous level, when the cursor dot indicates orange.

GOAL: Fill two boxes with specific colored pieces and rings to match a hidden pattern. CONTROLS: Click pieces to select, click slots to place, press space to verify. RULE: Rings count as two slots, allowing them to bridge gaps in the sequence. TRAP: Assuming rings occupy only one space leads to incorrect slot counts and failed matches.

GOAL: Place three rings in the empty box to define the order of three filled boxes, then complete each box with matching solid colors. CONTROLS: Click pieces to move them; click empty slots to place; press space to submit. RULE: The first item in each three-item group determines which ring goes in the outer box. TRAP: Assuming rings go into filled boxes; they actually act as separators for the empty container.

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells orange to satisfy hidden icon constraints. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color between red and orange. RULE: Each icon reveals the exact colors of the nine cells surrounding it. TRAP: Assuming icons only show majority colors; they actually dictate precise neighbors, requiring careful deduction.

GOAL: Shift colored blocks to match target zones using directional arrows. CONTROLS: Click red arrows to move blocks right; click green arrows to move blocks left. RULE: Each click shifts the adjacent block one step in the arrow’s direction. TRAP: Assuming green arrows are passive markers; they actively reverse red arrow movements.

GOAL: Place both dot-marked blocks onto their matching ring holes simultaneously. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the active block; clicking the inactive block switches control to it. RULE: Only the block currently controlled by arrows moves; the other remains stationary regardless of input. TRAP: Believing blocks auto-slide into holes; you must manually drive the second block into its target.

GOAL: Assign colors to grid cells to match hidden constraints. CONTROLS: Click a cell to cycle its color blue to red to orange. RULE: Center-colored cells must match the icon, while others must differ. TRAP: Believing every cell has one fixed target; ambiguous cells allow any valid alternative.

GOAL: Place two shapes on matching colors. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape. Space switches shapes. RULE: Shapes permanently take the color of any square they touch. TRAP: Thinking shapes must stay on their starting color; moving them dyes them permanently.

GOAL: Guide two distinct blocks to their matching colored exit gates. CONTROLS: Rotate the outer ring clockwise or counter-clockwise to shift block positions. RULE: Both blocks move simultaneously along the ring, maintaining their relative distance. TRAP: Assuming blocks move independently; rotating one block’s path also shifts the other’s position.

ESTABLISHED: The block moves freely in open grid cells. Red laser beams act as solid walls. The blue square is the target. FAILED: Attempting to move through red laser beams. Trying to reach the laser source directly. GOAL IS NOT: Reaching the red laser source. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block one step. Space interacts with adjacent objects.

GOAL: Slide the plug to cover the red pins at the far right. CONTROLS: Arrows move the entire plug one grid unit per press. RULE: The plug must align its tips precisely with the pin locations. TRAP: Moving right first causes a collision with the central white barrier.

GOAL: Slide the black shape so its mirror image perfectly covers the yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows move the shape; Space rotates it. RULE: Only the unrotated black shape reflects to match the yellow target’s orientation. TRAP: Believing rotation was necessary wastes moves; the solution requires pure translation.

GOAL: Transform the grid into a checkerboard pattern where even positions hold one color and odd positions hold the other. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell toggles its color and its immediate orthogonal neighbors, creating a ripple effect. RULE: Parity determines the target color; use the preview icons to confirm which color belongs to even versus odd coordinates. TRAP: Ignoring that preview icons occupy grid cells, leading you to waste moves trying to "fix" static markers instead of the board.

GOAL: Guide the plus shape to cover the blue target squares. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Shapes clip at board edges, allowing movement even when partially off-screen. TRAP: Assuming off-board parts vanish; they remain part of the shape’s footprint for coverage.

ESTABLISHED: Clicking podium tops toggles piece orientation. FAILED: Pushing boxes or moving dot to walls yields no progress. GOAL IS NOT: Simply aligning pieces or pushing blocks to edges. CONTROLS: Clicking different podium sections may trigger distinct rotations; UP is untested at walls.

GOAL: Position the mirror line so the black shape’s reflection perfectly fills the yellow silhouette. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the dashed line; other keys may adjust shape position or orientation. RULE: Reflections flip across the line’s axis; match the mirrored geometry to the target zone. TRAP: Assuming the line must pass through the yellow area; it must instead align with the black shape to cast the correct shadow.

GOAL: Merge two separate pieces into a single unit to fit inside the target circle. CONTROLS: Dragging a piece moves it; overlapping two pieces automatically fuses them into a larger shape. RULE: The fused shape must be fully contained within the circle's boundary to win. TRAP: Thinking you need to move pieces separately to the goal; they must merge first to satisfy the size constraint.

GOAL: Dial two-glyph tiles to target letters within a strict action budget. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate tile glyphs up or down to cycle through available characters. RULE: Tile width dictates glyph count; every seven units of width adds one rotatable character window. TRAP: Assuming the progress bar decreases one unit per action; it actually drops by half, misleading budget calculations.

ESTABLISHED: Orbit navigation works; RIGHT moves 0→45, DOWN moves 45→90, UP moves 90→45. FAILED: Attempts to move from 315 to 0 via UP or RIGHT resulted in no change. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clicking a color; the puzzle requires precise spatial alignment of the view. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the camera view; SPACE pours the selected color onto the block.

GOAL: Rotate camera to pour purple right, white top. CONTROLS: Arrows orbit view; Space pours; Click selects color. RULE: Each angle fills a specific half or quadrant. TRAP: Assuming all angles are connected; some moves are blocked.

GOAL: Route the plug to the core by clearing the red barrier with a wave. CONTROLS: Arrows move the plug; clicks trigger wave charges. RULE: Waves travel through open paths to destroy distant sockets and barriers. TRAP: The stem extends outside the main blob; moving right too early hits black voids.

GOAL: Align the moving line to match the target shape's reflection. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space cycles selection between the line and shapes. RULE: Only the object with white indicators responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Assuming the line moves with the shape; horizontal line moves are wasted actions.

GOAL: Align three distinct shapes to connect their pins. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected piece, Space rotates it, and clicks select new pieces. RULE: Connecting pins turns them gray, confirming a successful link between shapes. TRAP: Assuming rotation happens instantly without checking the new orientation before moving leads to misalignment.

ESTABLISHED: A 4-block vertical stack sits at columns 19-23 and 25-29, rows 36-55. Water surrounds these stacks. FAILED: Scanning for tip patterns and using segmentation nodes failed to correctly map the water boundaries around the stacks. GOAL IS NOT: The black cap at row 12 is not a solid barrier preventing vertical movement through the water. CONTROLS: Camera offset calculation was incorrect, leading to failed world coordinate conversions and misaligned planning.

GOAL: Paint the grid with specific colors based on position. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the pouring angle; Space pours the selected paint. RULE: Paint applies to the entire half defined by the angle, overwriting previous colors. TRAP: Trying to paint each region individually wastes time; use large overlapping pours to define boundaries efficiently.

GOAL: Place shapes to cover yellow targets, ensuring their reflections cover the mirror image. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected shape; Space cycles to the next shape. RULE: Shapes can overlap, and the target area calculation includes the intersection of overlapping pieces. TRAP: Assuming shapes cannot overlap leads to impossible positioning; the solution requires a nine-cell overlap.

GOAL: Move the square so its center lands on the target ring. CONTROLS: Click to move one piece; the other piece mirrors the movement relative to the center. RULE: The square’s position is always the midpoint of the two pieces; control their average to steer the square. TRAP: Focusing only on the active piece’s path; the mirrored piece’s route must also remain clear of obstacles.

GOAL: Reach the pink cross floating at the surface of the highest water pool. CONTROLS: Click blocks to remove them. Use arrow keys to steer the boat left or right. RULE: The boat automatically rises through any open vertical channel to the water level above. TRAP: Assuming the boat moves diagonally; it only rises straight up, requiring horizontal alignment first.

GOAL: Reach the exit with enough fuel to survive the trip. CONTROLS: Arrows move your character; stepping on rings refills fuel. RULE: Fuel drains per move, so you must collect rings to avoid running out. TRAP: Assuming rings are optional; skipping a refill guarantees failure before the exit.

GOAL: Move three blocks into their matching outlines to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows move the selected block; space rotates it; clicks select a block. RULE: Only one block is active at a time, so you must click to switch focus before moving each piece. TRAP: Clicking a block that is currently covered by another piece fails; ensure your target is visible and unobstructed.

GOAL: Move three separate objects to cover all yellow cells. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active object; space switched which object was active. RULE: Only the object with white highlights responds to arrow keys. TRAP: Moving objects in the wrong order wastes actions; switch to the last object only after the others are placed.
